data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"To test suppression by counting: count the lineage provenance of all accepted explanatory artifacts (A) and the lineage provenance of all *referenced* primitives in those artifacts (P). Calculate the cross-lineage reference ratio C = P_cross / P_total. If C is consistently zero or near-zero, and the system exhibits a high rate of within-lineage saturation (stagnation) signals, then suppression is occurring. If C is non-zero and proportional to the diversity of active lineages, it is efficiency.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Cross-lineage reference is not the only form of cross-cutting explanation; structural analogies may not require explicit primitive references.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Stagnation signals are not well-defined or are not recorded in the run's artifacts.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The diversity of active lineages is low (e.g., only one), making C trivially zero.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Cross-cutting explanations require the transfer of explanatory primitives across lineage boundaries. If ownership allocation suppresses these explanations, the flow of primitives across boundaries will be choked off. The count C measures this flow. The mechanism distinguishing suppression from efficiency is the presence of stagnation. Under an efficiency model, low cross-lineage flow is compensated by high within-lineage success. Under suppression, low cross-lineage flow co-occurs with within-lineage stagnation (the lineage is stuck but cannot reach outside for help).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
